result.summary: The pedestrian environment is largely underdeveloped, lacking sidewalks and accessible curb ramps. While a basic crosswalk and stop sign are present on the side street, pedestrians are forced to navigate unpaved shoulders or the roadway itself.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalks
hazards.description: The absence of sidewalks forces pedestrians to walk in the roadway or on uneven grass shoulders, increasing exposure to traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both sides of the main and side streets

hazards.name: Inaccessible Crosswalk
hazards.description: The marked crosswalk lacks curb ramps, creating a barrier for individuals with mobility impairments or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: At the ends of the white crosswalk lines on the side street

hazards.name: Sight Line Obstruction
hazards.description: Mature trees and utility poles near the intersection may partially obscure pedestrians from the view of turning motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the intersection near the stop sign

interventions.title: Sidewalk Construction
interventions.description: Install paved sidewalks on at least one side of the roadway to provide a dedicated, safe space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install compliant curb ramps with detectable warning surfaces at the crosswalk to ensure universal accessibility.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Upgrade
interventions.description: Replace the existing parallel line markings with high-visibility continental markings to improve driver awareness.

result.summary: The intersection lacks fundamental pedestrian safety features such as marked crosswalks, curb ramps, and a continuous sidewalk network. The environment is primarily designed for motor vehicles, with pedestrians forced to navigate unmarked crossings and unpaved shoulders on one side of the street.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: The intersection lacks any marked crosswalks, increasing the risk of pedestrian-vehicle conflicts at a point where people are likely to cross.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalks
hazards.description: The left side of the roadway lacks a paved sidewalk, requiring pedestrians to walk on the grass or in the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the main roadway

hazards.name: Vegetation Obstruction
hazards.description: Overhanging trees and dense bushes at the corner may limit visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns to clearly define pedestrian paths and alert drivers.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install curb ramps at all corners to ensure accessibility for all users, including those with mobility aids.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk network to the left side of the street to provide a continuous, separated path for pedestrians.

result.summary: The image shows a well-maintained concrete sidewalk separated from a commercial parking lot by a grass buffer and landscaping. While longitudinal pedestrian movement is accommodated, the environment is car-centric with no visible crossing infrastructure or traffic control devices.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from landscaping
hazards.description: Large coniferous shrubs adjacent to the sidewalk may block sightlines between pedestrians and drivers exiting the parking lot.
hazards.location_in_image: Left-center, shrubs between the sidewalk and the parking lot entrance area.

hazards.name: Unmarked driveway conflict zone
hazards.description: The sidewalk likely intersects with a parking lot entrance (not fully visible but implied by the lot) where no clear pedestrian priority is marked.
hazards.location_in_image: Mid-ground, where the sidewalk continues toward the building entrance.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style crosswalk markings across any driveway or parking lot entrances to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lighting along the sidewalk to improve visibility and safety for pedestrians during low-light conditions.

interventions.title: Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Trim or relocate large shrubs near the sidewalk/driveway interface to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The environment features a paved sidewalk on one side of a two-lane road, but lacks any marked pedestrian crossings or traffic control devices. The curved geometry of the road and lack of crossing infrastructure create a moderately hostile environment for pedestrians needing to traverse the roadway.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossing
hazards.description: There are no designated or marked areas for pedestrians to cross the two-lane roadway despite the presence of a sidewalk and commercial land use.

hazards.name: Limited sightlines
hazards.description: The curve in the road reduces the distance at which drivers can see pedestrians and vice versa, increasing collision risk.
hazards.location_in_image: Roadway ahead where it curves to the right

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a marked crosswalk with continental or ladder markings to designate a safe crossing point.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Warning Signage
interventions.description: Install 'Pedestrian Crossing' signs to alert drivers to the potential presence of people crossing, especially near the curve.
